Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 31.05.2012 passed in MVC No.838/2009 by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge & VI Additional MACT, Davanagere (for short 'the Tribunal'), the respondent No.3 therein has preferred this appeal.

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 30.07.2005, at about 5.00 p.m. the petitioner was travelling in a Mahendra passenger vehicle bearing No.KA 27 3546.
When the vehicle reached near Shibaragatti, the driver of the vehicle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner resulting in the vehicle turning turtle.
Because of the same, the petitioner suffered grievous injuries.
The offending vehicle was duly insured with the third respondent - Insurance Company.
The Tribunal, based on the evidence let in, has awarded a compensation of Rs.70,000/- along with interest @ 6% p.a.

Aggrieved by the same,
the third respondent - Insurance Company has preferred this appeal.
4. The case of the Insurance Company is that the offending vehicle was given the permit of a contract carrier and not that of a stage carrier.
However, the accident has happened when the vehicle was being used as a stage carrier.

However, it is admitted that the vehicle was duly insured The Branch Manager vs Mahendra B Jain on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111006006/
2 with the third respondent - Insurance Company and the quantum of compensation is not challenged.

sentences.text: 5. Inspite of service of notice, the petitioner before the Tribunal as well as the second respondent - owner have remained absent and notice to first respondent - driver has been dispensed at the risk of the third respondent - Insurance Company, who is the appellant herein.

6. Section 150 (2) (a) (i) (C) of the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 reads as under:-
"150. Duty of insurers to satisfy judgments and awards against persons insured in respect of third party risks.-
 (1) xxx  (2) No sum shall be payable by an insurer  under sub-section (1) in respect of any  judgment or award unless, before the commencement of the proceedings in which the judgment or award is given the insurer had notice through the court or, as the case may be, the Claims Tribunal of the bringing of the proceedings, or in respect of such judgment or award so long as its execution is stayed pending an appeal; and an insurer to whom notice of the bringing of any such proceedings is so given shall be entitled to be made a party thereto, and to defend the action on any of the following grounds, namely :-
(a) that there has been a breach of a specified condition of the policy, being one of the following conditions, namely:-
(i) a condition excluding the use of the vehicle -  (A) xxx  (B) xxx  (C) for a purpose not allowed by the  permit under which the vehicle is  used, where the vehicle is a  transport vehicle; or"
 7.
Based on the aforementioned provision, it is contended that the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: Ex.R2 is the permit granted to the offending vehicle and it shows that the permit granted to the offending vehicle is that of a contract carriage and not stage carriage.
The deposition of PW-1 shows that the vehicle was being used as a stage carriage and not contract carriage.
He has deposed that he was travelling in the vehicle from Byadagi to Ranibennur and that the vehicle was stopping at several places and the passengers were getting in and getting out.
Thus, the usage of the vehicle was in clear violation of Section 150 (2) (a) (i) (C) of the Motor Vehicles Act.
9. The Tribunal also in its order has concluded that the vehicle being used as a stage carrier when he had the permit of a contract carrier.

However, on the erroneous ground that if a vehicle is permitted to ply as a contract carriage, but plied as a stage carriage, it is for the Authorities to cancel the permit and the Insurance Company cannot escape liability.
The Tribunal has fastened the liability on third respondent - Insurance Company .

10. However, the learned Advocate for the Insurance Company in the course of the arguments fairly submitted, that when the vehicle is being used in violation of the permit, but had valid insurance,
then in that event, the Hon'ble Supreme Court as well as this Court in various judgments have held that Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation, but is granted the liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

11. It is seen that the Hon'ble Apex Court in AMRIT PAUL SINGH AND ANOTHER V. TATA AIG GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND OTHERS - reported in (2018) 7 SCC 558 and in several other judgments has held that in the case of violation of permit, if the vehicle is duly insured,
then the Insurance Company would be liable to pay the compensation to the claimants with liberty to recover the same from the insured.
12.

entities.text: AMRIT PAUL SINGH AND ANOTHER V. TATA AIG GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND OTHERS - reported in (2018) 7 SCC 558
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, in the instant case, under the given facts and circumstances of the case, the third respondent - Insurance Company shall be liable to compensate the petitioner and it will have the liberty to recover the same from the insured - second respondent - owner of the vehicle.

Hence, the following:-
ORDER i. The appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The third respondent - Insurance Company is held liable to compensate the petitioner as ordered by the Tribunal, with liberty to recover the said amount from the second respondent - owner of the vehicle.
iii. The judgment of the Tribunal is modified accordingly.
iv. The amount in deposit shall be transferred to the concerned Tribunal for disbursement.
v. Draw modified award accordingly.
